_source: Watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18 (Inside Decoded, 49K views, 1 month old; AI/altered-content label). Frames every 0.5 s for the first 4 s, then every 4-5 s, and a burst over the last 3 s; no sound probe (same channel as pBBBNOUxDh4). Shots approximate. Our own descriptions.

hook.firstFrame: a tall white board of pipes and red water tanks standing in a sunlit brick room; small caption mid-frame
hook.firstLine: This computer had no chips at all

shots.picture: the water-pipe machine in a brick room, wide
big white bold words slam in over the machine as the camera pushes in
macro: a column of red water running down a clear tube
the red stream pours into a brass cup, blue pill label at the top
a black-and-white archive-style photo card of an inventor beside his machine, name and year pill
close on red tanks and brass valves on the board, question pill
a glass tank on a stand filling with red water
water pumped to the top of the board
streams branching out of the main tank through side pipes
a cut-out curve card in a slot moves a valve, yellow pointer
the whole machine in the room again, a big headline at the top
red water spills across the floor from the base of the machine
a paper document card on a dark wood background, then a title appears under it
close on the board's pipes and tanks
the machine in the brick room as in frame one, under a subscribe card

lines.gist: it did maths with flowing water
an economics student built it in 1949, partly from bomber parts
water stands for money: pumped in as income, drained out as taxes and savings
swappable cut-out curves set the rules
it solved nine equations at once, and sometimes flooded the room
its inventor later drew one of economics' most famous curves

ending.lastFrame: the same water machine in the brick room as the first frame, subscribe card on top

whyItWorks: a contradiction in the first two words on screen (computer, no chips) slammed in huge at 0.5 s
a dive into the moving part (red water) by 1.5 s: motion and colour before any explanation
each idea is an equation written as a pill label: tank = running total, water = money
a comic beat (it flooded the room) before the payoff keeps the middle alive; it ends on frame one
